product: HubSpot CRM and Sales APIs (Developer Platform 2026-09)
description: HubSpot's cloud CRM and sales platform exposes date-versioned REST APIs for CRM records, properties, associations, search, engagements, and related marketing/content capabilities. The current public API reference is the 2026-09 release; HubSpot also provides an official remote MCP server for account data and a local Developer MCP server for CLI-based app development.

auth.summary: Supported credential families are distinct: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code credentials (client ID, client secret, authorization code, access token and refresh token); static-auth access tokens for a single-account app; developer API keys for the small set of documented developer-only endpoints; and a CLI personal access key for local CLI authentication. API calls use Bearer access/static tokens; OAuth client credentials are only for the webhooks journal API. A Super Admin or a user with Developer tools access can create a scoped account service key in Development > Keys > Service keys. Send it as a Bearer credential for REST calls.

HubSpot allows up to 10 developer test accounts per standard account; they include a 90-day trial of many enterprise features and expire after 90 days without API calls. App installation in a standard account requires the installing user to have HubSpot Marketplace access plus the permissions represented by requested scopes; MCP connector setup is performed in a HubSpot account.

interfaces.summary: The documented API interface is HTTP REST with JSON and Bearer authorization, rooted at https://api.hubapi.com and using date-based paths such as /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts. HubSpot maintains SDKs for Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby and .NET; the official CLI is npm package @hubspot/cli. MCP is a separate Streamable HTTP interface at https://mcp.hubspot.com plus a local CLI-launched Developer MCP server.

mcp.summary: HubSpot publishes two first-party MCP servers: a remote CRM/data server at https://mcp.hubspot.com and a local Developer MCP server installed through the HubSpot CLI. The remote server supports OAuth with mandatory PKCE, respects user permissions, exposes read/write CRM and activity/content tools, and blocks conversation access when Sensitive Data is enabled; users must reinstall if connector scopes change. The local server is for developer-platform/CLI tasks and uses CLI authentication. The official Composio catalog also lists a HubSpot toolkit with OAuth2/API-key auth, 355 tools and 2 triggers; it is a third-party toolkit, not a HubSpot-maintained MCP server.

buildability.summary: The private route is buildable by wrapping the REST API with static auth in one standard account (or OAuth in up to 10 allowlisted accounts), ideally starting in a free developer test account. The public route is an OAuth app with a hosted OAuth backend and Marketplace distribution; after the unlisted install cap it needs listing/review/AUP approval. A builder can alternatively reuse the official remote MCP for user-authorized CRM actions or the local Developer MCP for CLI/developer tasks. All routes require a HubSpot developer/account context and appropriate scopes; gated features require the corresponding subscription/scope.

evidence.support: OAuth is required for multiple accounts and requires a hosted OAuth backend; static auth is for a single authorized account.

integration.credential_setup: Create a current Developer Platform app/project and choose auth/distribution in app-hsmeta.json. For OAuth, configure at least one HTTPS redirect URL (localhost HTTP is permitted for testing), required/optional scopes, client ID and client secret, and host an OAuth callback/token backend. For a static app, install it in the target account and copy the generated access token. Legacy private apps cannot be newly created after 2026-10-26, so do not use that legacy creation path for a new build. A Super Admin or a user with Developer tools access can create a scoped account service key in Development > Keys > Service keys. Send it as a Bearer credential for REST calls.
integration.wire_auth: Send API calls to https://api.hubapi.com with Authorization: Bearer <OAuth access token or static access token> and JSON. OAuth token exchange/refresh uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST bodies. Developer API keys are only for documented developer-key endpoints and are passed as hapikey (often with appId). A Super Admin or a user with Developer tools access can create a scoped account service key in Development > Keys > Service keys. Send it as a Bearer credential for REST calls.
integration.oauth_flow: OAuth 2.0 authorization-code: redirect the user to HubSpot consent, receive a single-use code on the registered redirect URI, exchange it for tokens, store token metadata securely, send the access token as Bearer, and refresh before expiry. The only documented app-level client_credentials flow is for the webhooks journal API.
integration.oauth_endpoints: Authorization: https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize. Current versioned token endpoint: POST https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/2026-09/token for grant_type=authorization_code or refresh_token; the same endpoint supports client_credentials for webhook-journal app tokens. Token introspection: POST https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/2026-09/token/introspect.
integration.scope_and_refresh: Scopes are space-separated in the authorization request and configured as required, optional or conditionally required. The current exchange returns scopes, hub_id and expires_in=1800; access tokens last 30 minutes. Refresh uses grant_type=refresh_token with client_id, client_secret and refresh_token. Optional scopes can be omitted when the portal/user lacks access and then are absent from resulting tokens; connector scope changes require MCP reinstallation.
integration.test_setup: Create a free developer test account from a standard account (up to 10; 90-day inactivity expiry) and use it as the isolated test portal. For CLI development install Node.js 20+ and @hubspot/cli, then run hs account auth; for remote MCP create a connector, register the redirect URL, and test with MCP Inspector using Streamable HTTP, OAuth and PKCE.
integration.live_setup: For one live standard account use a private/static app and its generated token. For multiple selected live accounts use private OAuth with an allowlist (10 accounts by default). For broad distribution use marketplace OAuth; sign the AUP, use the sample install URL, and submit a listing for manual review. Pre-listing marketplace OAuth is limited to 25 non-test installs; after listing it is unlimited. Private OAuth defaults to 10 customer portals. An app created in an eligible Solutions Partner portal can reach 100. Private static auth is limited to one standard portal. Marketplace review removes the 25-install cap.
integration.distribution_requirements: Current app-hsmeta.json distribution is marketplace or private. Marketplace requires OAuth; private can use OAuth for allowlisted accounts or static auth for one account. OAuth redirect URLs must be HTTPS except http://localhost for testing. Marketplace listing requires a public setup guide, proper single-app OAuth identity, only needed scopes, terms agreement and manual Ecosystem Quality review; Super Admin is required to submit.
integration.base_url_and_version: API root is https://api.hubapi.com. The current API reference is date-version 2026-09, with paths such as /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts and /crm/objects/2026-09/{object}/search. HubSpot says new integrations should use the latest date version; legacy endpoints remain documented separately.
integration.resource_families: CRM object records and schemas/properties; associations; search; batch and import/export; engagements (calls, emails, meetings, notes, tasks); owners/users/account; pipelines; conversations; marketing/content/campaigns; files/CMS; webhooks and webhooks journal; OAuth/authentication. The MCP adds CRM, activity, content, conversation, marketing email, social and account-context tools, subject to permissions and subscription.
integration.api_reference_or_spec: Reference: https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/overview and the linked versioned guides. HubSpot also publishes per-product OpenAPI 3.0 JSON specs in https://github.com/HubSpot/HubSpot-public-api-spec-collection, but its README says the collection is for internal Postman synchronization, proprietary and not licensed for external use; it is not a single consolidated 2026-09 external bundle.
integration.mcp_endpoint_or_install: Remote data MCP: Streamable HTTP at https://mcp.hubspot.com; create an MCP connector in HubSpot, copy client ID/secret and configure a PKCE-capable MCP client. Local Developer MCP: install @hubspot/cli (CLI >=8.2.0) and run hs mcp setup, selecting Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, VS Code or Windsurf.
integration.mcp_coverage: Remote read tools cover CRM records (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, leads, users, custom objects, lists and beta revenue objects), activities, content/marketing, analytics, communications/conversations, email/social and account context. Write tools cover CRM records/activities, content, campaigns, drafts, pipelines, properties, associations, custom objects, segments and social; sensitive-data/conversation restrictions and user permissions apply. Developer MCP covers local HubSpot Developer Platform/CLI app and CMS tasks. Composio's catalog match is a third-party HubSpot toolkit with 355 tools/2 triggers.
integration.blocker: New builds cannot use the legacy private-app creation flow (sunset 2026-10-26). A public marketplace build is gated by account/developer setup, correct scopes, AUP, HTTPS callback/backend and manual Ecosystem Quality review; before listing, installs are capped at 25. Remote MCP is gated by a current Developer Platform MCP connector, user-granted permissions and PKCE. Feature-specific gates include subscription tiers and scopes.
integration.blocker_next_step: Create or obtain a standard HubSpot account with a free developer test account, create a current Developer Platform app, choose private/static for a single-account prototype or private/marketplace OAuth for distribution, configure the minimum CRM scopes, and run the documented contacts read/search fixture. For MCP, create the connector and test get_user_details in MCP Inspector before implementing writes. Obtain Super Admin/Marketplace access and the relevant paid subscription only when the chosen object/feature requires it or when submitting/listing publicly.
integration.edition: HubSpot CRM and Sales / standard HubSpot account using the current Developer Platform API reference (2026-09); legacy private/public app creation is sunset but existing legacy apps remain supported.
integration.region_and_deployment: Cloud SaaS. HubSpot documents the single API root https://api.hubapi.com and remote MCP endpoint https://mcp.hubspot.com rather than regional API base URLs. OAuth token metadata includes a hublet field (for example na1) and hub_domain, but the checked public docs do not specify a selectable region/deployment base URL; region routing is therefore unresolved beyond HubSpot-managed hublets.
integration.credential_identity: client_id/client_secret identify the Developer Platform app; authorization code is a one-use handoff; access token authenticates calls for the installing user/account; refresh token renews access. OAuth introspection returns app_id, client_id, user_id, user email, hub_id and hub_domain. Static auth token is the single-account app credential; developer API key identifies the developer/app for special endpoints; CLI Personal Access Key authenticates local CLI commands. A Super Admin or a user with Developer tools access can create a scoped account service key in Development > Keys > Service keys. Send it as a Bearer credential for REST calls.
integration.tenant_or_org_id: The tenant is the HubSpot account/portal identified by hub_id (Hub ID); OAuth metadata also returns hub_domain, user_id and app_id. The installing user's permissions and granted scopes determine accessible data.
integration.minimum_plans_by_route: No single paid minimum is stated on the core contacts/companies/deals/tickets object guides; standard accounts may be free or paid, with access controlled by product subscription, permissions and scopes. Developer test accounts are free with a 90-day trial of many enterprise features. Documented feature gates include Revenue Hub Professional/Enterprise for beta quote MCP tools and Marketing Hub Professional/Enterprise for AEO; free tools cannot create custom pipelines. Confirm the target object/endpoint's scope and account entitlement before production.
integration.operation_inventory: Count unknown. The current 2026-09 API reference exposes families through versioned guides (CRM objects/search, properties, associations, engagements, account, conversations, marketing/content, automation, webhooks and more); the CRM search guide explicitly lists 19 object search families plus engagements. The official OpenAPI 3.0 repository contains per-product/rollout JSON files and is updated by HubSpot, but its README says it is internal/proprietary and not a consolidated external 2026-09 specification. No total operation count is asserted.
integration.official_sdks_and_clis: Official SDKs: Node.js, Python, PHP, Ruby and .NET (HubSpot-maintained); Go is explicitly community. Official CLI is @hubspot/cli, installed with npm and used via hs commands including hs api, hs account auth, hs project and hs mcp setup.
integration.composio_toolkit: Composio catalog match: HubSpot toolkit, latest catalog version 20261116_01, OAuth2 and API Key auth, 355 tools and 2 triggers. It documents managed OAuth and custom HubSpot OAuth config, including a Composio callback URL and scope matching; this is a third-party toolkit rather than HubSpot MCP.
integration.mcp_auth_status_restrictions: Remote MCP uses OAuth with mandatory PKCE; connector permissions are derived from available tools and user-granted permissions, and all actions respect HubSpot user permissions. Reinstall after scope changes. Sensitive Data blocks conversation access through MCP; social writes require social.publish; beta/revenue and AEO features require documented scopes/subscriptions. Local Developer MCP uses the CLI's local authentication. MCP Inspector is a community-maintained test client, not a HubSpot data server.
integration.private_and_public_routes: Private/static: current Developer Platform app with distribution=private and auth=static, one standard account at a time plus up to 10 developer test accounts. Private OAuth: distribution=private/auth=oauth, hosted backend and 10 accounts by default. Public/marketplace: distribution=marketplace/auth=oauth, hosted backend, AUP and listing review; up to 25 non-test installs before listing and unlimited after listing. Do not treat legacy private/public app creation as a current route because both creation flows are sunset in 2026, although existing legacy apps remain supported. Private OAuth defaults to 10 customer portals. An app created in an eligible Solutions Partner portal can reach 100. Private static auth is limited to one standard portal. Marketplace review removes the 25-install cap.

actions.intent: List contacts for an initial read-only integration test
actions.required_inputs: Bearer token; optional query parameters limit (maximum 100), after, properties, propertiesWithHistory and associations.
actions.outputs: JSON object with results[] contact records (id, properties, createdAt, updatedAt, archived) and optional paging.next.after/link.
actions.scopes: crm.objects.contacts.read (the guide lists this or the write scope; read is sufficient for this action).
actions.pagination: Use limit<=100; follow paging.next.after in subsequent GET requests until no next value.
actions.documented_example: The Retrieve all contacts section gives GET /crm/objects/2026-09/contacts?limit=50 and a response with paging.next.after=33452.

actions.required_inputs: Bearer token and JSON body {"properties":{...}}; at least one of email, firstname or lastname is required. Optional associations use to.id and associationCategory/associationTypeId.
actions.outputs: Created contact record, including its record ID and properties (the guide's request fixture uses email=example@hubspot.com, firstname=Jane, lastname=Doe).
actions.pagination: Not applicable to a single create; batch create is available separately and limited to 100 records.
actions.side_effect: Creates a CRM record and may create associations; customer data mutation, so require explicit user confirmation in an agent.
actions.documented_example: Create contacts with property values fixture: {"properties":{"email":"example@hubspot.com","firstname":"Jane","lastname":"Doe"}}.

actions.required_inputs: Bearer token and JSON body with optional filterGroups/filters, properties, sorts, limit (default 10, maximum 200) and integer after; example filter uses propertyName=email, operator=CONTAINS_TOKEN, value=*@hubspot.com.
actions.outputs: JSON with total, results[] records and optional paging.next.after; each result includes id, properties, createdAt, updatedAt and archived.
actions.scopes: A CRM scope is required; for contacts use crm.objects.contacts.read for read search.
actions.pagination: Default 10 per page; set limit up to 200 and pass paging.next.after as integer. Search queries are capped at 10,000 total results and 5 requests/second per account.
actions.documented_example: The Make a search request section provides a contact email filter fixture and response with total=2, results and paging; pagination and limits are documented later on the page.

description: Intapp DealCloud is a cloud deal and relationship-intelligence platform for professional firms, with site-specific REST APIs for schema, data, administration, backups, publications, and Relationship Intelligence. The current publisher documentation also describes a vendor-hosted MCP server for the DealCloud with Celeste license.

auth.summary: The REST API uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials. An API-enabled DealCloud user supplies the site URL, client ID, and API key/secret to the token request; the resulting bearer token is sent in Authorization. The public docs use both “API key” and “client_secret” terminology, so the exact mapping of the issued secret to those names should be confirmed in the customer site Swagger/credential screen.

evidence.support: The docs state OAuth2 Client Credentials, require client_id and client_secret in a form-encoded token request, and say to use the returned bearer token.

integration.credential_setup: Have a DealCloud administrator assign the intended user to a group with the API capability in Admin > User Management. The user then opens Profile, enables API Key, and copies the API key. Collect the customer site URL and the client ID/secret terminology used by that site; the current Python SDK config uses siteUrl, clientId, and clientSecret. Keep the secret out of source control.
integration.wire_auth: POST {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret/API key, and space-separated scope. Use the response access_token as Authorization: Bearer {token} on subsequent REST calls.
integration.oauth_flow: Service-to-service OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials; it is not a user authorization-code flow for the REST API. The token page says the access token expires after 900 seconds (15 minutes); obtain a new token by repeating the client-credentials request.
integration.oauth_endpoints: REST token endpoint: {baseUrl}/api/rest/v1/oauth/token. No separate REST authorization endpoint is documented for client credentials. MCP uses standard .well-known OAuth discovery, but the public MCP docs do not spell out the tenant-specific authorization and token URLs.
integration.scope_and_refresh: Documented REST scopes are user_management (management), data (data and schema), publish (publications), ri_import (Relationship Intelligence), and backup (backups). Request only needed scopes. The public token docs document 15-minute expiry and repeat-grant renewal, not a refresh-token lifecycle; specialized/deprecated scopes include provider_sync, api, data_provider, and exchange.
integration.test_setup: Use an existing customer site host and API-enabled user. Test token and REST calls in the site Swagger at https://{host}/swagger or import https://{host}/swagger/current into Postman. Start with schema discovery, then a read-only rows call. No public sandbox, seed tenant, or anonymous test credentials are documented.
integration.live_setup: Use the same site-specific host for live data, with an API-enabled user whose group permissions cover the target endpoints and records. For MCP, configure Tools > MCP Servers, use the default or a published custom server, and connect through OAuth; writes require Enable Write Tools and appropriate user permissions.
integration.distribution_requirements: Private/customer distribution requires the customer site, issued credentials, API capability, and least-privilege group/data permissions. Vendor MCP hosted clients are documented; local Claude Code/Codex CLI/Cursor desktop use localhost redirects that must be enabled by the Account Manager. Custom or third-party MCP clients require contacting the Account Manager. No anonymous public API distribution route is documented.
integration.base_url_and_version: Use the customer site as base host: https://{host}. Core data and schema are versioned /api/rest/v4; OAuth and much administration/Relationship Intelligence routes are /api/rest/v1. Swagger is /swagger and its machine-readable current spec is /swagger/current on the customer host. Publications are now site-specific, replacing the older environment/region endpoint structure.
integration.resource_families: Publisher docs cover authentication, user management, schema, data (cells, rows, history, files/reports), backups, publications/event streaming, and Relationship Intelligence. The current Python SDK additionally documents files, history, template reports, merge, and publications helpers.
integration.api_reference_or_spec: Official API reference: https://api.docs.dealcloud.com/docs. The docs say each customer host exposes Swagger at https://{host}/swagger and OpenAPI at https://{host}/swagger/current. integration.mcp_endpoint_or_install: No package install is required for the hosted server. An admin copies the endpoint from Tools > MCP Servers; the default format is https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud. Paste that URL into a compatible client and authorize through OAuth. Custom servers require a published Schema Contract and MCP Server.
integration.mcp_coverage: Official tools cover name lookup, record search/details, current user and tenant profile, GraphQL schema introspection/query composition/execution, truncated-result pagination via read_more, entry-form rules, choice/reference/user value lookup, validation without saving, and submit_entry. The default server exposes the full site schema; a custom server scopes objects/fields through a Schema Contract. Writes are disabled until explicitly enabled.
integration.blocker: The material blockers are customer access and product gates: REST needs a customer site plus API-enabled user/credential; the host-specific Swagger/spec cannot be inspected generically; MCP needs DealCloud with Celeste, Manage MCP Servers/Celeste Member/MCP Access capabilities, and write enablement for writes. actions.intent: Discover and read records from a DealCloud object
actions.required_inputs: Customer host; OAuth bearer token with data scope; entryTypeId (object API name such as company or numeric ID). Optional query, fields, resolveReferenceUrls, wrapIntoArrays, dateTimeBehavior, skip, and limit.
actions.outputs: JSON object containing totalRecords and rows; each row contains EntryId and the requested object fields, with references represented as DealCloud reference objects unless resolved.
actions.scopes: data; the token docs say data is required for Data and Schema APIs.
actions.pagination: Use totalRecords, skip, and limit; start at skip=0 and limit=1000, increment skip by limit, and continue until all records are read. The documented maximum limit is 10,000; an out-of-range page returns 200 with an empty rows array.

actions.intent: Create new CRM records in bulk
actions.required_inputs: Customer host; OAuth bearer token with data scope; entryTypeId; JSON array of up to 1000 entries. Each new EntryId must be negative (for example -1); choice and reference fields must use IDs.
actions.outputs: JSON array of created entries with assigned positive EntryIds and normalized field values.
actions.scopes: data; endpoint permissions are also controlled by the API user’s DealCloud group/data permissions.
actions.pagination: No response pagination; bulk request is capped at 1000 entries. Split independent batches as needed, while using negative IDs to link entries within one batch.
actions.side_effect: Creates records in the customer site; this is a write operation and should be used only with explicit customer authorization.
actions.documented_example: The docs POST two Address records with EntryId -1, street values, company ID 3713810, and AddressType ID 1782017; the response returns EntryIds 18604301 and 18604302.

actions.intent: Discover the site’s object/schema model before mapping CRM fields
actions.required_inputs: Customer host and OAuth bearer token with data scope; no path or query parameters.
actions.outputs: JSON array of site EntryTypes/objects, including apiName, singularName, pluralName, entryListType/subtype, id, name, and entryListId.
actions.scopes: data; the token docs state data is required for Schema APIs. Schema requests are limited to 5 calls per second.
actions.pagination: The documented endpoint has no parameters and the example returns the full list; no pagination mechanism is documented for this call.
actions.side_effect: Read-only; schema APIs do not modify the site schema.
actions.documented_example: GET {{host}}/api/rest/v4/schema/entrytypes with Bearer token returns entries such as Company (id 2014), Campaign, and Attachment.

description: Plaid is a vendor-hosted financial-account connectivity and data API platform. Its public developer platform combines Plaid Link for end-user institution connection with a JSON/HTTPS API for Items, accounts, balances, transactions, identity, investments, liabilities, payments, risk and other financial workflows. The normal build flow is server-side link-token creation, client-side Link, backend public-token exchange, then product calls using an Item access_token.

integration.credential_setup: Create/verify a Plaid Dashboard account. Obtain the team client_id and the matching Sandbox or Production secret from the Keys area. Keep both server-side. In the Link flow, create a link_token, let the client run Link, receive the short-lived public_token, and exchange it server-side for access_token plus item_id. Sandbox can create a public_token without Link via /sandbox/public_token/create.
integration.wire_auth: Plaid API requests are HTTPS JSON POSTs with Content-Type: application/json and TLS 1.2. Almost all routes accept client_id and secret in the JSON body or PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET headers. Item product calls carry access_token; OAuth/MCP calls use a Bearer OAuth access_token.
integration.oauth_flow: Bank OAuth is an end-user Plaid Link flow: Link redirects the user to the financial institution, then the institution returns the user to Link/application. This is distinct from Plaid’s own OAuth service for customers/partners/services. The latter supports client_credentials, refresh_token and RFC 8693 token-exchange grants.
integration.oauth_endpoints: Plaid documents POST /oauth/token, /oauth/introspect and /oauth/revoke on the Plaid API. Dashboard MCP examples call https://production.plaid.com/oauth/token; the remote MCP endpoint itself is https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/.
integration.scope_and_refresh: OAuth scopes documented by Plaid are user:read, user:write, exchange and mcp:dashboard. OAuth access tokens are short-lived (the published example has expires_in 900); use refresh_token with grant_type=refresh_token to refresh. This is separate from Item access_token, which does not expire by default but can be rotated with /item/access_token/invalidate or revoked by /item/remove.
integration.test_setup: Use https://sandbox.plaid.com with Sandbox secret and test credentials user_good/pass_good. Sandbox is free, supports unlimited test Items, and has Sandbox Studio. For automated tests, POST /sandbox/public_token/create with institution_id and initial_products, then POST /item/public_token/exchange. The local official Sandbox MCP can mock data, create tokens and fire webhooks.
integration.live_setup: Request Production access in the Dashboard or apply for Trial if eligible. Current public docs say Trial is free for new US/Canada teams created on/after 2026-04-15, allows 10 Production Items, and exposes a limited product set. Before live OAuth bank connections, complete Production approval, compliance-center registration and any institution-specific OAuth registration; complete Link setup before the first Production Item.
integration.distribution_requirements: Never ship client_id/secret or long-lived Item access_token to the client. Distribute only link_token to the Link client and send public_token back to the backend for exchange. For bank OAuth, register/allowlist redirect URIs; Production requires HTTPS (Sandbox permits localhost HTTP), and mobile platforms have additional package/universal-link registration requirements.
integration.base_url_and_version: Sandbox base URL: https://sandbox.plaid.com. Production base URL: https://production.plaid.com. The fetched official OpenAPI spec declares both servers and info.version 2020-09-14_1.822.2; the repository README identifies API version 2020-09-14. Treat that as the published API/schema version, not a promise of a semver-stable endpoint contract.

integration.mcp_coverage: Dashboard MCP covers five documented tools: plaid_debug_item, plaid_get_link_analytics, plaid_get_tools_introduction, plaid_get_usages and plaid_list_teams. They provide Item diagnostics, Link funnel/conversion/error analytics, usage/API volume metrics, guidance and team discovery. Local MCP covers mock financial data, Plaid-doc search, Sandbox access tokens and webhook simulation. Neither is a drop-in replacement for the full 350-route customer API.
integration.blocker: The principal blocker for live/customer builds is access approval: Production access must be requested/approved, products and countries may need separate enablement, OAuth bank connections require compliance registration, EU/UK customers need Custom plans, and several products are Custom-only. Dashboard MCP additionally requires a team approved for Production with at least one product. Secure handling of secrets and consumer financial data is also mandatory.

Official Link SDKs: iOS, Android, React, React Native and Flutter, plus Web/Hosted Link docs. integration.mcp_auth_status_restrictions: Dashboard MCP: team must have Production approval for at least one Plaid product; create OAuth token with client_credentials and scope mcp:dashboard at /oauth/token, pass Bearer token to the Streamable HTTP endpoint, refresh after its documented 15-minute expiry. Dashboard MCP is production-only, diagnostics/analytics-oriented, actively changing and limited-support. Local Sandbox MCP is client-local and test-oriented; Composio’s Plaid MCP is a third-party catalog integration.
integration.private_and_public_routes: Private backend route: hold client_id/secret and Item access_token server-side, call REST/SDK directly, and receive webhooks. Public/client route: initialize Link with link_token in web/mobile/Hosted Link, let the end user authenticate, return public_token via onSuccess, then exchange it on the backend. This division supports public applications without exposing long-lived credentials.

actions.intent: Initialize an end-user Plaid Link session for a new Item or permitted update flow.
actions.required_inputs: client_id, secret, client_name, language, country_codes, user.client_user_id (or user_id), and products for a new Item; optionally webhook, redirect_uri and product-specific options.
actions.outputs: link_token and expiration; the Link session later returns a public_token via onSuccess.
actions.scopes: No OAuth scope; requires Plaid API credentials and account/product/country enablement. User consent is collected in Link for the selected products.
actions.side_effect: Creates a Link token and configures the session. The end user grants consent later in Link.
actions.documented_example: Plaid Node example uses user.client_user_id, client_name "Plaid Test App", products ["transactions"], country_codes ["US"], language "en", webhook and redirect_uri, then client.linkTokenCreate(request).

actions.intent: Turn a successful Link result into the persistent Item credential used by backend product calls.
actions.required_inputs: client_id, secret and public_token from Link onSuccess (or Sandbox /sandbox/public_token/create).
actions.outputs: access_token, item_id and request_id. public_token expires after 30 minutes; access_token does not expire by default.
actions.scopes: No OAuth scope; the access_token authorizes calls for the specific linked Item and only products enabled/consented for the account.
actions.side_effect: Creates/activates the Item access credential for later reads; does not initiate a payment or transfer.
actions.documented_example: Plaid Node example sets { public_token: publicToken }, calls itemPublicTokenExchange, and reads response.data.access_token and response.data.item_id; the docs also show an access-sandbox fixture.

actions.intent: Read initial transaction history or incremental transaction changes for an Item.
actions.required_inputs: client_id, secret, access_token; cursor is null/omitted on first sync, then next_cursor; optional count (1–500), options and account_id.
actions.outputs: accounts plus added, modified and removed transaction arrays, next_cursor, has_more, request_id and transactions_update_status.
actions.scopes: No OAuth scope; requires an Item with Transactions initialized or product access that allows the endpoint, plus user authorization obtained through Link.
actions.pagination: Cursor loop: process each response, continue while has_more using next_cursor, persist the final cursor; on pagination mutation error restart from the first cursor for that update.
actions.side_effect: Read-oriented; first call may trigger Plaid preparation/initialization of transaction data and related webhooks, but it does not mutate bank funds.
actions.documented_example: Plaid Node fixture initializes cursor from storage, loops while hasMore, concatenates added/modified/removed, assigns next_cursor and persists updates; response fixture shows accounts, arrays, next_cursor and has_more.

product: Gemini Notebook for business (assignment: NotebookLM Enterprise)
description: Google Cloud's enterprise-ready, source-grounded research and writing notebook. Users add documents and other sources, then query, chat, summarize, and generate notebook artifacts; the enterprise deployment keeps notebook data in the customer's Google Cloud project and adds IAM, identity, residency, compliance, and administrative controls. Current Google documentation uses “Gemini Notebook Enterprise” and “Gemini Notebook for business” while the supplied name is NotebookLM Enterprise.

auth.summary: The documented API uses a Google OAuth 2.0 user access token sent as an Authorization: Bearer header. API reference pages accept cloud-platform, discoveryengine.readwrite, and discoveryengine.serving.readwrite; source batchCreate additionally accepts discoveryengine.assist.readwrite. The how-to uses gcloud user credentials and says the REST methods require an authenticated user with an active Notebook Enterprise license. No API-key, personal-token, Basic, or product-token mechanism is documented for this product API.

evidence.support: Create requires cloud-platform, discoveryengine.readwrite, or discoveryengine.serving.readwrite and discoveryengine.notebooks.create.
REST methods require an authenticated user account with an active Gemini Notebook Enterprise license and the example uses gcloud auth print-access-token.
Google OAuth 2.0 returns access/refresh tokens and the access token is sent as Authorization: Bearer.

test_access.summary: A testable path exists through Google Cloud: create/select a project with billing enabled, enable Discovery Engine API, configure an IdP, grant Cloud NotebookLM Admin/User roles, obtain a full-featured 14-day free-trial subscription, assign the user a region-specific license, and use user OAuth credentials. API calls still require an active license, so this is not an anonymous sandbox.

evidence.support: The free-trial tier is a full-featured 14-day trial subscription of 5000 licenses.

evidence.support: Setup requires a Google Cloud project with billing enabled and Discovery Engine API enabled.

production_access.summary: Live access is licensed and project-administered. Paid monthly or annual subscriptions are available; subscriptions are region-specific and require at least 15 licenses (up to 5,000). Administrators configure identity, enable the API, grant roles, and assign licenses. In-country locations are GA with an allowlist and require contacting the Google account team; standard regional access is documented separately. The free trial is time-limited, not a general free production tier.

interfaces.summary: Primary developer interface is a versioned REST API over HTTPS using Google API gRPC-transcoding paths and JSON. Official Google Cloud client libraries are available for the Discovery Engine service ecosystem (Go, Java, Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP, C#), while docs provide curl and gcloud auth/print-access-token examples. A project-specific web UI is also part of the product. No NotebookLM-specific gcloud command group is established by the checked CLI reference; gcloud notebooks is a different command group for environments, instances, locations, and runtimes.

integration.credential_setup: Create a Google Cloud OAuth client (client ID and client secret) for a web/server application, register an exact redirect URI, request Discovery Engine scope(s), and obtain user consent. Alternatively use gcloud auth login and gcloud auth print-access-token for operator/user testing. Customer project must have Discovery Engine API enabled; Google Drive sources additionally require gcloud auth login --enable-gdrive-access.
integration.wire_auth: HTTPS JSON REST with Authorization: Bearer <Google OAuth access token> and Content-Type: application/json. Resource names embed project number/ID, location, notebook ID, source ID, or audio-overview ID. OAuth client secret and refresh token are secondary secrets; neither is sent in API calls.
integration.oauth_flow: Authorization Code grant for confidential web/server app: redirect user to Google consent with response_type=code, scope, client_id, redirect_uri, and state; exchange code for tokens; call API with access token. Workforce Identity Federation/Cloud Identity configures enterprise web UI sign-in but does not replace the API Bearer token.
integration.oauth_endpoints: Authorization: https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth. Token/code-exchange and refresh: POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. Google OAuth documentation specifies these endpoints and HTTPS-only use.
integration.scope_and_refresh: API method scopes are cloud-platform, discoveryengine.readwrite, or discoveryengine.serving.readwrite; sources.batchCreate also accepts discoveryengine.assist.readwrite. Request access_type=offline for refresh token; access tokens expire and refresh tokens obtain new access tokens until revoked/expired. Composio defaults to https://www.googleapis.com/auth/discoveryengine.readwrite and manages refresh/rotation.
integration.test_setup: Create/select project, verify billing, enable discoveryengine.googleapis.com, configure one IdP (Cloud Identity or supported OIDC/SAML Workforce Identity Federation), grant Cloud NotebookLM Admin for setup and Cloud NotebookLM User to tester, obtain 14-day free trial, assign license in target multi-region, then gcloud auth login. For Drive sources use --enable-gdrive-access.
integration.live_setup: Buy paid monthly or annual subscription in chosen multi-region, assign enough licenses, maintain Cloud NotebookLM Admin/User IAM, and distribute project/region-specific notebook.cloud.google.com URL or call REST endpoints. API calls must use licensed user and matching project/location.
integration.distribution_requirements: Private/internal: customer-owned Google Cloud project, billing, Discovery Engine API, IdP, IAM, and region-specific active license. Public SaaS/agent distribution: each customer must authorize Google OAuth and have access to licensed Enterprise deployment; public OAuth apps requesting sensitive/restricted scopes may require Google verification. External OAuth apps in Testing restrict sign-in to test users and refresh tokens expire after seven days.
integration.base_url_and_version: Published machine-readable and REST reference version is v1alpha. Global examples use https://discoveryengine.googleapis.com/v1alpha/projects/{PROJECT}/locations/{LOCATION}/...; docs also show region-prefixed hosts for us/eu and a US multi-regional transport host discoveryengine.us.rep.googleapis.com with LOCATION=us. API is gRPC-transcoded REST with JSON.
integration.resource_families: Notebook management: projects.locations.notebooks. Sources: projects.locations.notebooks.sources. Media: projects.locations.notebooks.audioOverviews. Notebook resource contains source metadata and optional CMEK metadata.
integration.api_reference_or_spec: Official REST reference: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1alpha/projects.locations.notebooks; source reference: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1alpha/projects.locations.notebooks.sources; audio reference: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1alpha/projects.locations.notebooks.audioOverviews. Recursive count of methods under projects.locations.notebooks is 10: notebooks 5, sources 3, audioOverviews 2.

description: An open-source, local Node.js command-line tool for Mermaid. It renders Mermaid definition files to SVG, PNG, or PDF, can replace Mermaid blocks in Markdown with generated SVG references, and can also be invoked through a Node.js API or container. The exact edition researched here is the public npm package 12.2.0; it is not Mermaid Chart SaaS.

auth.summary: No runtime API credential, account, OAuth flow, or tenant identity is required for the local CLI. Installation uses public npm/container distribution and invocation is through local process arguments, stdin, and files.

evidence.support: The documented install and invocation are npm install plus `mmdc -i ... -o ...`, with no login/token step.
Source parses local CLI options and reads UTF-8 files or stdin; it has no auth/header handling.

test_access.summary: Test access is local and account-free: install globally or locally with npm, use npx, or run the documented Docker/Podman image against a mounted fixture.

evidence.support: Documents global npm install, local install, npx, Docker, Podman, and a mounted `/data` example.

production_access.summary: Production access is self-hosted/local, CI, or container execution. The npm package is public and the CLI has no SaaS plan, approval, or region gate.

evidence.support: The package is marked “Public”.
Documents local npm and container deployment routes.

interfaces.summary: Primary interface is the `mmdc` CLI; the package exports a Node.js API (`run`, `renderMermaid`, `cli`, `error`), and Docker/Podman provide container invocation.

evidence.section: Usage; Use Node.JS API; Alternative installations
evidence.support: Shows `mmdc`, `import { run }`, and Docker/Podman commands.
Exports `run`, `renderMermaid`, `cli`, and `error`.

mcp.summary: No direct vendor MCP endpoint or install is documented for the exact CLI. A separately maintained community `mcp-mermaid` server supports Mermaid rendering locally; the official hosted Mermaid MCP is a different Mermaid Chart product and requires account authentication.

evidence.support: Maintainer repository documents `npx -y mcp-mermaid`, transports, and Mermaid diagram rendering.
Official hosted endpoint is `mcp.mermaid.ai` and every tool call requires Mermaid authentication; this is Mermaid Chart MCP, not the CLI.
The upstream package documents file and container rendering. Its README does not identify a project-operated MCP endpoint.

buildability.summary: Buildable as a local CLI wrapper or container job without credentials. Start sandbox-first because the package launches Puppeteer/Chromium; use the documented Puppeteer config escape hatch when a system browser is required.

evidence.support: Provides Docker/Podman routes and an already-installed-Chromium troubleshooting link.
Documents `--puppeteerConfigFile` and `executablePath`.

integration.credential_setup: No runtime credential setup. Install the public package (`npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`, or local/npx/container equivalent) and invoke `mmdc`; only local files/stdin/config paths are supplied.
integration.wire_auth: None. This is a local process interface: Commander parses argv, `getInputData` reads UTF-8 from an input file or stdin, and outputs bytes/files.
integration.oauth_flow: Not applicable: the CLI has no OAuth grant or login flow.
integration.oauth_endpoints: Not applicable: no authorization or token endpoint exists for the local CLI.
integration.scope_and_refresh: Not applicable: no OAuth scopes, refresh token, access-token lifetime, or refresh lifecycle is used.
integration.test_setup: Create a small `.mmd` fixture and run `mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.svg`; alternatively pipe a definition with `--input -`. Use local npm, npx, or a container.
integration.live_setup: Run the pinned npm binary in CI/production or use Docker/Podman with the diagram directory mounted at `/data`. For an existing browser, pass a Puppeteer JSON config with `executablePath`.
integration.distribution_requirements: Public npm/npx and container routes are documented. The repo also lists GHCR and warns that Homebrew installation is no longer supported. Technical gates are compatible Node, Puppeteer/browser, and readable/writable filesystem paths; there is no account gate.
integration.base_url_and_version: No base URL because there is no hosted API. The current public npm page reports @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 12.2.0. Upstream master source separately exposes version 12.0.0 and depends on Mermaid ^12.2.0; pin npm 12.2.0 rather than relying on a floating tag.
integration.resource_families: Mermaid `.mmd` definitions; Markdown/`.markdown` files containing Mermaid fences; stdin; Mermaid JSON config; CSS/themeCSS; optional Iconify icon packs; and SVG, PNG, PDF, or transformed Markdown outputs.
integration.api_reference_or_spec: Use the upstream README and `src/index.js` Commander/JSDoc as the reference. The CLI is not a REST/GraphQL service, so no OpenAPI/GraphQL schema is applicable; source exports the Node API and defines the CLI options.
integration.mcp_endpoint_or_install: No MCP endpoint belongs to the exact CLI. For the separate community server, install/run `mcp-mermaid` via npx or npm; its documented local endpoints are `http://localhost:3033/sse` and `http://localhost:1122/mcp`.
integration.mcp_coverage: Community mcp-mermaid validates/renders Mermaid and supports base64, SVG, Mermaid text, file, svg_url, and png_url output modes, but its manifest uses `mermaid-isomorphic` and Playwright rather than @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli. Official Mermaid Chart MCP exposes validation/rendering plus project/diagram management, but is a separate hosted product.
integration.blocker: No credential or plan blocker. The practical blockers are Node >=22.13.0 in upstream package metadata, Puppeteer ^25.0.0 as a peer dependency, a compatible Chromium/browser, and local filesystem permissions.
integration.blocker_next_step: Pin @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli 12.2.0, install prerequisites, run the documented SVG command and a PNG/PDF smoke test, then containerize if needed. If bundled Chromium is unavailable, supply `--puppeteerConfigFile` with `executablePath` and validate the output in the target environment.
integration.vendor: Mermaid open-source project / mermaid-js; npm scope @mermaid-js.
integration.edition: Open-source public npm package @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli version 12.2.0, distinct from Mermaid Chart SaaS.
integration.region_and_deployment: Region-neutral local workstation, CI, or container deployment. No vendor-hosted region or tenant deployment is specified.
integration.credential_identity: None at runtime; execution is under the local OS process/user. npm registry access is distribution-time only.
integration.tenant_or_org_id: Not applicable; the CLI has no tenant, organization, workspace, or account identifier.
integration.minimum_plans_by_route: Local npm/npx, Docker/Podman, and self-hosted source routes require no product plan or account. The separate hosted Mermaid MCP route requires a Mermaid login but documents the free Basic tier as sufficient.
integration.operation_inventory: No network-operation count applies. Source inventory: one `mmdc` CLI entry point, four exported programmatic symbols (`run`, `renderMermaid`, `cli`, `error`), and rendering families for single definitions, Markdown extraction, stdin, and SVG/PNG/PDF outputs. Count method: direct source export statement plus branches in `run`/`renderMermaid`.
integration.official_sdks_and_clis: Official CLI: `mmdc`. Official programmatic Node API: `run` (plus `renderMermaid`, `cli`, `error` exports). No separate language SDK or remote API client is documented. Upstream excludes its Node API from semantic versioning guarantees.
integration.composio_toolkit: Composio has a Mermaid Chart MCP catalog entry with one “Validate and render mermaid diagram” tool. It is not an exact @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli toolkit match.
integration.mcp_auth_status_restrictions: Exact CLI: no MCP auth restrictions because it is not an MCP server. Official hosted Mermaid MCP: every tool call requires authentication, via OAuth 2.1/dynamic client registration or a manual Mermaid token; free Basic account is documented. Community local mcp-mermaid documentation shows stdio/SSE/streamable setup without a credential field.
integration.private_and_public_routes: Public route: npm/npx, public repository, and documented containers. No private vendor route is documented. An organizational fork/self-hosted private build is possible but inferred from the public source/license, not a vendor-managed private edition.
